mappings._doc_justification:
NetSuite Customer.currency stores a reference to a Currency record (the internal id of the joined currency, not the ISO code itself). The migration target on Rootstock is the ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR') — Salesforce multicurrency convention. Two valid Rootstock targets:

  (a) Standard Salesforce CurrencyIsoCode (the SF multicurrency platform field, present on every multicurrency-enabled object)
  (b) Custom Currency_Code__c (a Rootstock-package custom field that mirrors the ISO code)

For this calibration the gold target is Currency_Code__c (the Rootstock-custom field) since Rootstock implementation guides historically reference it by name. The TRANSFORMATION is non-trivial: NetSuite's currency field stores a record ID; the migration must JOIN to the Currency record to extract the ISO code. This is captured by combination_type='single' with the understanding that the transform layer handles the lookup; the field-pair is still 1:1.

gold.notes:
Difficulty: medium. The complexity isn't the field-pair (still 1:1) but the JOIN required to extract the ISO code from NetSuite's currency-record reference. An AI that proposes this mapping correctly should have access to the Currency record's ISO code field via context-builder's schema introspection. The combination_type stays 'single' because at the field-pair level it's a 1:1 mapping; the transform layer (PR 10.5b can add a separate transform example) handles the JOIN.

The judgment-call axis: target field name. CurrencyIsoCode (standard SF) vs Currency_Code__c (Rootstock custom). The schema flags this for Kaan's review.
